title: Optional pseudonymous usage and performance statistics
objective: Plan a once-only desktop opt-in notice and Settings controls, full-app timelines of typed events with periodic performance samples, linked by a random persistent installation ID, a per-launch session ID and a keyed per-image ID in Develop and approved OS/app/CPU/GPU/memory context, with no PII, IP tracking or photo/metadata information; deliver bounded best-effort HTTPS batches to api.luxforge.app with an open-source local backend reference and final native/privacy evidence.
context_summary: The owner requested planning only: explicit once-only consent, full-app usage/import/performance counts, api.luxforge.app, quiet best-effort background batching and Settings opt-in/out. The additional instruction requires a unique persistent ID, app/OS versions and CPU/GPU/device details for performance diagnosis/targeting, with no PII, IP addresses or photo/metadata information. On 2026-10-09 the owner added that a usage timeline linking one installation's or session's events in order is acceptable and useful as long as there is no PII; the owner then asked for a stable per-image ID in Develop, removed the hourly and daily caps, and asked for a disclosure that says only that events are tracked for debugging and analytics, with no PII. The design therefore uses timed, sequenced typed events, a random in-memory session ID per launch, a random opt-in installation ID stable across launches, cleared on successful opt-out, bounded approved device fields, no photo-derived labels and pseudonymous rather than fully anonymous reporting. Protocol is delegated: finite HTTPS JSON batches and a self-hosted Vector/ClickHouse/Grafana reference. Protected host authority prevents ordinary clients enabling consent; production reporting needs a packaged clean build and a checked-in activation switch that stays off until the real endpoint passes the deployment checklist; no durable report queue or replay exists. IP-based logging, hashing, enrichment and rate limiting are excluded at every hop; packet routing addresses necessarily exist but never become statistics/log records. Routine types/layout/static event/model mapping and backend packages are delegated within docs/design/usage-statistics.md. Implementation awaits a separate instruction; the roadmap high-tier minimum and current-main re-review apply. Consent, the event registry and independent ingress are initially runnable; working local client delivery precedes final native/performance/backend activation qualification. Real DNS/TLS/hosting and absent private RAW/native inputs affect only live/final qualification and stay unrun. Proposed services/ paths are future outputs. No further question/approval/research task is inserted.

tasks.description: Implement protected persistent usage consent, the once-only startup claim and schema-described host commands.
extra_context: Produce the authoritative consent store and runtime generation/eligibility seam consumed by TASK-004 and TASK-007; no desktop notice or network delivery in this task.

Extend the existing bounded preferences store with the current usage_statistics record. Missing means off/unasked; unsupported/malformed data is refused unchanged. Persist a disabled prompt claim before returning show_prompt, using the configuration lock so concurrent processes have only one winner.

Register usage.read, usage.prompt.claim and usage.set with the ordinary mutation envelope. Enable requires existing ClientAuthority permission authority and the exact current disclosure version; ordinary clients may disable. Generic preferences.set/null cannot change or reset this protected record.

Disable the runtime gate before an off write and stay off if it fails; enable only after successful persistence. A duplicate earlier enable must not reapply consent after revocation. Read/claim failures fail closed without rewriting files.

Define process-wide host eligibility so debug/developer, hidden/background/evidence/test and headless hosts remain off; isolated test eligibility is explicitly injectable and cannot use the production destination. Statistics data classes/destination changes invalidate enabled consent without resetting prompt_shown.

Add no preferences file watch or polling. Expose an off-owner stored-record read that the worker uses before detaching a window and before every network handoff: a stored opt-out or an installation ID different from the in-memory one ends the generation, clears buffers and stops producers, so another process's revocation is never followed by an upload.

Implement build identity and activation as the design states: cargo xtask package embeds the clean source revision at build time, the release is the version plus the revision's first 12 hex characters, and unrevisioned or dirty builds are ineligible. Add one checked-in production activation switch, off; while it is off every launch is ineligible (no claim, notice, Privacy tab or collection) and usage.read reports inactive destination. Explicit test eligibility with a loopback receiver works without the switch or a packaged build. Do not turn the switch on.

Generate a cryptographically random UUIDv4 only on successfully persisted enable; store it with consent, reuse it across launches/upgrades/catalog changes, clear it on successful opt-out and create a fresh ID on later opt-in. Failure cannot silently replace or expose the old ID. The same persisted enable creates a 32-byte random image_key stored and removed with the installation ID; usage.read and preferences.read never return it. Include this lifecycle in schemas and local read state; never log IDs or the key.

acceptance_criteria: Absent consent, ineligible hosts, read failures and scope-version mismatch collect/send nothing; existing preferences, catalogs and recipes are preserved.

Two instances over one retained writable configuration produce exactly one new prompt claim; duplicate requests, relaunch, dismissal bookkeeping and catalog changes never create another automatic claim.
Schema discovery describes every new operation and authority requirement. Untrusted enable and generic-preference/reset bypasses are rejected; authorized enable persists before taking effect.
Off is immediate even on persistence failure, effective/stored state is honest, and stale/deduplicated replies cannot re-enable a revoked generation.

Consent changes reach the local supervisor and open clients; a stored opt-out or changed installation ID from another process ends this process's generation at the next pre-detach or pre-handoff check, with no watch or polling timer.

No ID exists before agreement; an enabled ID survives relaunch/upgrade/catalog change, is cleared on saved opt-out, and rotates on a later opt-in without causing another prompt. Failed writes preserve the file and fail closed in process.

With the activation switch off, or in an unrevisioned or dirty build, usage.read reports the fixed reason and no claim, notice, collection or network work occurs; a packaged build reports version+12-hex revision, and explicit test eligibility still works over loopback.
The image key exists exactly while an installation ID does, rotates with it, and never appears in a read, schema example, log or event.

steps: Add focused core/store/owner authority, concurrent claim, retry-after-revoke, read-only/corrupt file and generation tests using isolated roots.
Use network/producer spies to verify every suppressed host case performs zero work; inspect schemas and all generic reset paths.
expected_results: Focused consent tests pass; no real consent, external endpoint or image data is touched.

tasks.description: Implement the typed event/device registry, bounded event banks and strict pseudonymous wire encoder with privacy fixtures.
extra_context: Produce the producer/snapshot interface consumed by TASK-004, TASK-005 and TASK-006, plus checked-in current schema and synthetic valid/invalid examples. This is executable implementation of the design contract, not another contract-review task.

Resolve the finite built-in tool/operation enum against current shipped modules. All strings originate in static enums; do not expose arbitrary event JSON, command arguments, module descriptors, IDs or labels.

Implement fixed-size event records (typed name, enum fields, bounded integers, session sequence number and session-relative millisecond time) in two banks of at most 512 events each. Combined statistics buffers/control/serialized capacity is 256 KiB; one body is 64 KiB and 512 events. A full bank or contention drops the event, counts it in dropped and still consumes its sequence number. State must not grow with image count or time offline.

Producers accept an eligibility/generation seam, do bounded non-blocking work and drop on contention/full capacity. Disabled producers allocate nothing. Worker serialization and snapshotting cannot hold a producer on a blocking lock.

Emit only the current envelope (installation ID, session ID, session_start to the second, batch_seq, dropped, release, device) and events in seq order with exactly their registry fields. To meet the body size, omit process.sample events first and then the newest events, counting them as dropped; never create a second request or partial document.
Keep client encoding strict and backend validation independent; fixtures must describe only the latest schema. No compatibility library, general telemetry SDK or server dependency enters the core.

Encode exactly one canonical UUIDv4 installation ID, one in-memory UUIDv4 session ID created when collection becomes effective in a launch (new per launch and per off/on, never persisted), the 32-hex image field on the events the design lists (HMAC-SHA-256 under the image key over the catalog fingerprint, truncated to 16 bytes, implemented over the locked sha2 crate with RFC 4231 test vectors) and a device profile capped at 2 KiB: app/OS versions, architecture, normalized CPU vendor/model/core counts, memory capacity band and at most two existing GPU adapter model/backend/version profiles. No free-form system strings, hardware UUIDs/serials, IPs or photo resolution/format labels. Profile capacity is included in the 256 KiB total. TASK-006 supplies validated probe values. The release field is the bounded version+12-hex-revision string from TASK-001.

All allocation capacities obey the stated caps under producer floods, contention and oversized windows; disabled mode creates no collector storage.

Producers cannot block or perform filesystem/network/formatting work; lost observations remain local diagnostics.

steps: Add focused event-bank, ordering, sequence-gap, generation, concurrent flood and capacity tests, with independently written expected batches.
Inspect typed producer signatures and run privacy sentinel/schema-negative fixtures; reconcile application-owned allocation capacity separately from thread/TLS overhead.
Exercise canonical ID/device fixtures, unknown/raw model/driver/version strings, at-most-two GPU profiles, device-context size and profile-change generation tests.
expected_results: Registry/encoder/bounds tests pass with deterministic synthetic data and no network.

tasks.description: Build the standalone stateless ingestion validator for the chosen HTTPS batch contract.
extra_context: Proposed output: services/usage-ingest/, a standalone Rust package with its own empty [workspace] table and Cargo.lock outside the root workspace, so desktop builds, core tests and cargo xtask check gain no server dependency. Extend the repository's pinning, notice and advisory checks to its lockfile. The HTTP framework is delegated; project code remains GPL-3.0-or-later.

Implement POST /v1/usage/batches, strict latest-only decoding, content/body/depth/event-count/range/field and seq/t ordering checks and whole-batch rejection. Backend implementation can proceed independently from the client using the design's contract; TASK-011 later reconciles actual client fixtures.

Accept no account or embedded desktop secret. Bound public-route concurrency, time, global limits and downstream buffers. An optional bounded rate limiter may use the approved reporting ID with 15-minute expiry, but never IP addresses or hashes, even transiently. Do not retain IPs, headers, bodies, reject payloads or installation/session IDs in logs/traces.

Normalize an accepted batch into one row per event (installation ID, session ID, session_start, batch_seq, seq, t, event name and registry fields, server receive time to the second) and one release/device profile per session, replaced when a later batch carries a changed profile. No raw body, photo data or other identifier is forwarded. IDs appear only in the approved private bodies/rows.

Return an empty 202/204 for bounded in-memory acceptance without promising durability; refuse/drop on pressure. Forward once to the private collector and do not add a durable ingest spool. Replies cannot alter desktop consent or collect more data.
Prepare a local fake downstream and functional tests; DNS, certificates and production deployment are not inputs to this task.

tasks.description: Connect consented event windows to one bounded background sender using the existing transport.
extra_context: Consume TASK-001 consent/generation/eligibility and TASK-002 snapshots. Use capabilities::transport::Transport with luxforge-net's existing HttpTransport and cancellable JobControl; no second HTTP/TLS stack or analytics SDK.

Create at most one statistics worker/request, entirely off owner/UI/Rayon. Fixed destination is https://api.luxforge.app/v1/usage/batches; redirects/cookies/auth/compression are absent. Tests inject loopback transport/config and cannot contact production.

Implement nonempty scheduling at ten minutes after a window's first event or at 512 events, plus 0-60 s jitter, with attempts at least 60 seconds apart and no hourly or daily request or byte cap (owner, 2026-10-09); 64 KiB bodies, 1 KiB response bodies and 2/2/5 s timeout limits. A window that fills before the next attempt is allowed drops further events. Increment batch_seq for every detached batch, including ones later discarded, so losses are visible.

Drop every detached batch after its one attempt, including ambiguous failures. Apply the fixed fresh-data cooldown, 429 Retry-After clamp and terminal 3xx/other-4xx session suspension; no health check or retry of previously sent bytes.

Respect native visibility, 30-minute oldest-contribution expiry and generation cancellation. Empty/disabled/hidden states have no send timer, and no worker event wakes the UI. Use the TASK-001 stored-record read before detaching and immediately before each network handoff; an opt-out or changed installation ID discards everything in this generation.

Quit cancels/discards without joining a network operation on the UI close path; preserve existing preference-close behavior. Cross-process revocation and failed off writes must keep the effective runtime off.

Include the already cached bounded device context and persistent reporting ID in ordinary batches; there is no metadata handshake or extra device endpoint. Do not put the ID in URLs/headers/logs. Drop or detach an old-profile window on adapter changes without forcing an early request; off clears all profile buffers.

acceptance_criteria: Fake-clock tests prove jitter, 60-second minimum spacing under event floods, the absence of any hourly/daily cap, one in-flight request, no empty batches, no catch-up burst and bounded long-offline memory.
Success, 408/429/5xx, DNS/TLS/socket failure, redirects, unsupported endpoint/schema and oversize responses obey the policy; ambiguous bodies are never retransmitted.
Before-consent, headless/evidence/hidden/background/debug modes create no real network activity; current revoked data is absent after off/on.
Opt-out while serialization/resolution/connect/write/read is active prevents later handoffs and cancels the current JobControl under transport bounds; late callbacks cannot restart it.
Closing never waits for an upload, and sending/sampling status adds no GUI messages, redraws, status-bar warnings or connectivity probes.

tasks.description: Instrument shipped operations at their authoritative boundaries, with a checked-in coverage inventory.
extra_context: Deliver a checked-in coverage inventory (proposed docs/engineering/usage-statistics-coverage.md) mapping every current user-facing command/action and GUI-local workspace operation to an approved typed producer or explicit read/internal/privacy exemption.

Emit at authoritative shared success/transaction boundaries, not a click log or serialized events.since. Deduplicated retries emit once, automatic sub-operations do not emit a second user operation, and GUI/shortcut/palette/API paths converge on the same events.

tool.commit means one event per built-in group a committed transaction changed, never draft ticks or parameter values. images.added carries the count of newly committed original photo rows per add operation; reopening, directory indexing, skipped/failed rows and thumbnails add nothing. Export's operation.end carries the count of completed outputs. Also emit session.start, app.presented, app.idle, workspace.enter, image.open, interaction and preview.settled as the design defines them, with the image field exactly where the design lists it. Compute the image ID once when a photograph is adopted, from the catalog fingerprint already held, never from a file read, filename or metadata.

Cover Select/Develop navigation, masks/brush/gradients, history/versions, presets/copy-paste, catalog organization/Locate, settings and available batch paths. Do not prebuild metrics for future editing modules or export formats.
Publish durations/outcomes from existing asynchronous completion seams with the consent generation captured at start. Pre-consent or revoked in-flight work must not appear in a later generation.
Use the core's disabled sink until host integration is ready, so this task does not depend on the sender or desktop notice.

The no-photo-information instruction removes all source format/resolution/size/camera labels, filenames and metadata: events record what kind of operation happened, when, and in Develop the keyed image ID, never anything that names or describes the photograph, and no editing values.

tasks.description: Add consented low-frequency process performance sampling and the approved CPU/GPU/OS/memory device context.
extra_context: Produce process.sample events and the validated device profile consumed by TASK-002's encoder and TASK-004's batches. Use the core's disabled sink until host integration, so this task depends on neither the sender nor the desktop notice.

At most once per minute of presented activity, reuse a fresh existing process report or sample through the same process-wide sampler on the statistics worker. Coordinate freshness with the Performance panel so its system calls are not duplicated; preserve memory kinds and omit unavailable or reset counters. The first CPU/GPU read is a baseline; reset it after hiding, sleep or consent changes. No sleep backfill, per-frame or per-tile stream, and no new GPU or CPU image work.

Gather the device context once per opted-in launch on a worker through safe platform metadata and the already selected renderer/tile adapter info. Normalize numeric OS/driver versions, CPU/GPU model families, logical/physical cores and memory bands; omit unrecognized strings. Never query hardware serials/UUIDs or network interfaces, create a GPU device, run external commands or poll inventory. Refresh only on existing adapter/path changes, and never relabel observations gathered on a prior adapter.

tasks.description: Add the non-blocking startup notice and Settings Privacy controls through the shared consent commands.
extra_context: Consume TASK-001 commands and effective/stored consent. Show a startup notice only after the usable workspace and a successful durable claim; do not steal focus or block editing/import/native dialogs.

Use the design's short disclosure (events are sent for debugging and analytics and never include name, contact details, IP address, photos, filenames or photo metadata) and two neutral actions, Share statistics and No thanks. Escape/close is refusal; a crash or closing before presentation does not cause another automatic prompt.

Add a Privacy tab, switch, the same short disclosure and a collapsed What is sent list of the event, ID and device fields to existing Settings. Use usage.set, not direct preferences writes or UI-only booleans. Show effective off and actual save failures without a delivery status/warning UI.
Preserve existing General/Appearance/Experiments behavior and scaling/accessibility. Settings reflects consent changed through the command service; there is no generic reset or hidden enable path.

Extend the existing evidence step/state model and settings smoke path with isolated explicit test eligibility. Production traffic must remain disabled in every automated run; use an injected local receiver at integration.
Routine compact notice placement/styles are delegated within the non-modal, accessible contract; no foreground UI automation is authorized.

The disclosure says only that events are tracked for debugging and analytics and what they never include (owner, 2026-10-09); it never claims the reports are anonymous or contain no personal data. The collapsed list names the installation, session and image IDs and device fields. Successful opt-out removes the local ID and image key; existing backend events expire after 90 days.
The notice and Privacy tab exist only in eligible launches; with the activation switch off, ordinary builds show neither, while explicit test eligibility shows both.

Completed-work quick and rendered tiers pass within their recorded scope, with retained evidence; local client delivery does not wait for later qualification.

steps: Run one isolated multi-launch background settings/usage journey with state/log/capture and local transport evidence, including API/GUI event parity and a revoked upload.
Review the complete diff, schema discovery, originals preservation and performance checklist; run final quick and rendered tiers. Record unavailable corpus evidence explicitly.

tasks.description: Prepare the pinned Vector, ClickHouse and private Grafana reference stack with bounded device/profile retention and no IP tracking.
extra_context: Proposed output: services/usage-statistics/ with pinned local compose configuration, normalized numeric-row tables/queries, dashboards and a runbook. No production provisioning or deployment.

Connect TASK-003 private normalized ingress output to Vector HTTP source/ClickHouse JSONEachRow. Keep raw public bodies out of Vector and analytics; bound memory and queues without an unbounded/durable request spool.

Persist only the approved per-event rows (installation ID, session ID, session_start, batch_seq, seq, t, event fields, receive time to the second) and per-session release/device profiles; expire events, sessions and profiles at 90 days. Queries deduplicate on (session_id, seq). No photo attributes, raw bodies or additional key; no indefinitely retained device inventory.

Configure every hop/log/trace/database query logger to exclude IPs, reporting IDs, header/body values and rejected payloads; forward no X-Forwarded-For/cookies. Disable access/security logs, CDN/WAF analytics, IP-based limiters and third-party analytics. Global or bounded reporting-ID rate limits are permitted. Dashboard/database/collector access is private and authenticated.

Provision feature/import/export/outcome/active-time/timing/resource views grouped by app/OS/CPU/GPU/memory cohorts, a per-session timeline view, simple path queries (for example adding images to Develop to a completed export, and what precedes a failed operation) per-image histories across an installation's sessions, and per-installation history for performance debugging. Explain opt-in bias, loss and the missing session tail, and label sessions and installation IDs as such, never unique people/physical devices; no account join or photo lookup; image IDs from different installations are unrelated.
Backend capacity, finite shared-NAT-friendly rate limits, storage engine/query arrangement and exact pinned packages are delegated. Preserve license notices; do not claim deferred manual audits.

This work depends on the normalized ingress rows, not desktop delivery or an external account. A local container runtime may be unavailable: prepare all artifacts and record its integration test as unrun until execution is possible, never substitute inspection for a pass.

tasks.description: Qualify native responsiveness, storage/traffic bounds and source preservation after working client delivery.
extra_context: Run after feature integration on a quiet M4 in release mode with generated 24 MP/60 MP photographs and available authentic RAW inputs. Compare opted-out and opted-in behavior with fast/slow/offline local receivers.

Measure producer p50/p95, input-to-frame distributions, idle/hidden CPU, process memory, resource-sampling overhead, TLS/thread-stack overhead, request/body volume and close latency; include drag floods, imports, exports, long cooldowns and opt-out.

Targets are unmeasured planning budgets: producer p95 <10 microseconds and no sustained interactive latency regression >max(1 ms, 5%). Fix regressions and repeat only affected checks before the final integrated run.

Prove app-owned statistics capacity <=256 KiB independently of measured TLS/stack overhead. Record request volume with no hourly/daily cap under typical editing and event floods, and validate the 60-second spacing and bounded windows with long fake-clock/flood tests and a real traffic capture; no timing assertion dependent on shared-host load in ordinary unit tests.

Run finished-work quick and the appropriate timing/full verification with the available corpus scope. Full milestone acceptance requires the actual corpus/native evidence; missing owner manifests or Windows/Linux native hardware remain explicit, without blocking TASK-008 delivery.
Record current measurement scope/results in the performance spec/design and feature status, not a historical run log. No production reporting or user consent is used for measurement.

Verify OS/CPU/GPU/driver/profile gathering adds no UI/owner latency or extra GPU device, the profile fits its 2 KiB cap, and actual metadata probes match approved model values without capturing raw system strings. Generated 24/60 MP images are local verification inputs only; their sizes/formats never enter telemetry.

tasks.description: Verify actual client-to-reference-backend privacy and protocol behavior, and prepare the production activation handoff.
extra_context: Exercise TASK-008 encoded batches through TASK-009 local stack; reconcile client registry/schema fixtures with the independent ingress validator and actual normalized rows.

Test accept/reject, sent-once loss/ambiguous failures, rate/size/cooldown behavior, storage expiry and no metadata retention across all components. Use synthetic opted-in isolated clients, never real users' statistics.

Produce a concrete deployment/activation checklist and synthetic live-endpoint probe using the implemented contract, with DNS/TLS/route/rate/privacy/retention checks. The probe and deployment instructions must exist before any external deployment request.

Production DNS/certificates/hosting and turning on the activation switch are external or separately authorized actions outside this request; the checklist names the switch change as its last step. Do not provision, publish or probe a nonexistent production API. Record live delivery as unverified until a real deployment satisfying the disclosure exists.
This final backend/activation handoff has no dependency back into the working client. It contains no owner-approval or research task; production changes require a separately authorized action.

Include actual current installation/device fields in acceptance and negative fixtures. Prove ID lifetime/rotation, no photo-derived labels and no IP logging, hashing, enrichment, forwarded metadata or rate-limit state at every hop, including infrastructure defaults. Network packet routing addresses are unavoidable and are not statistics.
